title: Cap. VII: No circular proof — death entered with its cause, not unique imputed act
pass_a_gloss: Placeus rejects Garissoles's circular reading of the fifth reason. The learned author of that reason never claimed that Romans 5:12 is a proof that everyone is doomed to death. Read again the reason as Garissoles recited it in § XI and as Placeus transcribed it: nothing there yields that consequence cleanly. Paul would not labor to demonstrate what Scripture, every age's experience, and the entire human race already confess out loud. Nor would he prove what is clearer (that all die) by what is darker (that all have sinned). So verse 12 is not a proof of death. Its point is preventive: to keep readers from thinking people die for one man's single sin charged to them by imputation, Paul states that through one man death entered the race in such a way that sin — death's cause — entered with it. Death therefore falls on each immediately for his own implanted sin drawn from Adam, not immediately for Adam's one actual act. Garissoles fabricates a circular demonstration where the text has none.
pass_b_english: And yet the most learned author of that reason did not say that the Apostle in verse 12 is proving that all are sentenced to death. Reread, I ask, and consider the reason as it had been recited by Garissoles himself at § XI and copied out by me. Do you notice anything of the kind in it? Or can a sound consequence be drawn from it? Why indeed would the Apostle have set about proving what Scripture, and the experience of every age, and the whole human race besides, forever confess and cry aloud? Who also would believe that the Apostle meant to prove the clearer by the obscurer? For that all die is clearer than that all have sinned. He does not, therefore, prove; but lest all men should seem to die on account of one man's one sin imputed to them, he affirms that through one man death so entered the human race that not death alone invaded all men, but also its cause — sin. And so all die not immediately on account of that one actual sin of one man, but on account of each man's own implanted in him, derived from that one. Doctor Garissoles therefore invents a circular proof where there is none.
source_text: Atqui non dixit illius rationis eruditissimus autor, Apostolum versu 12. probare, omnes esse addictos morti? Relege quaeso & considera rationem, quemadmodum ab ipso Garissolio recitata fuerat § XI. & a me exscripta. Num tale quid in ea animadvertis? aut ex ea bona consequentia deduci potest? Eccur vero Apostolus id probare instituisset, quod Scriptura, & omnium seculorum experientia, genusque adeo humanum universum perpetuo confitetur & clamat? Ecquis etiam credat, Apostolum probare voluisse clarius per obscurius? Clarius enim est omnes mori, quam omnes peccasse. Non igitur probat, sed ne viderentur omnes homines ob unicum unius hominis peccatum eis imputatum mori, affirmat per unum hominem ita mortem ingressam esse in genus humanum, ut non sola in omnes homines invaserit, sed ejus etiam causa, peccatum. Itaque mori omnes non proxime ob unum illud actuale unius hominis peccatum, sed ob suum quemque sibi insitum, ab illo derivatum. Fingit ergo D. G. probationem circularem ubi nulla est.
